title: Tracing bill-of-materials — weekly sketch & handoff
body:
Context:
This is a working sketch for the observability weekly — focused on the idea of a 'Tracing bill-of-materials' (BoM): list of trace signal components, their unit cost, and mitigation options. Goal: create a single page that SREs and product engineers can use to plan trace budgets and make quick tradeoffs when onboarding new routes/models.

Meeting summary (2027-03-08 standup + async notes):
- Quick sync (15m). Attendees: Maya, Evan, Jules, Priya, Samira.
- Primary focus: two parallel experiments — adaptive sampling tied to cost SLOs (OBS-4321) and a low-cardinality dashboard variant for product teams.
- Notable incident: small but noisy trace spike on 2027-03-06 03:12 UTC after model v1.8 rollout; correlated with longer kv-cache initialization in serving-runtime. Root cause hypothesis: new attention kernel interaction with cache warming.

Agenda items discussed:
1) Tracing BoM prototype (Maya)
   - Draft BoM columns: signal (span, event, metric), estimated token/spans-per-request, retention tier, rough cost-per-100k, sampling knobs available, downstream consumers.
   - Action: fill example rows for chat/generation/embedding routes. Evan to produce numbers from billing proxies by EOD Fri.
2) Adaptive sampling experiment (Jules)
   - Design: dynamic sampler that lowers full-span retention for high-volume routes when 7-day cost projection > budget threshold. Implementation tied to sampling policy service; can toggle per-route feature flag.
   - Success criteria: 30–50% reduction in traced-span volume for target routes with <5% loss in actionable debugging sessions (measured via manual eval set of 40 incidents).
3) Dashboard lightweight view (Priya)
   - Product asked for a single 'latency-cost' widget they can embed in dashboards without exposing full traces. Idea: aggregate trace-derived metrics pre-joined and truncated; provide link to full trace only when needed.
   - UX: default view shows p50/p95 latency, estimated token cost, sampled trace-count. Toggle to expand to full trace list.
4) Cost telemetry runbook updates (Samira)
   - Add entry: how to temporarily throttle trace ingestion per route using admin API + expected fallout. Draft steps included below.

Decisions made:
- Keep 30-day backfill window for critical routes but move lower-volume routes to 7-day by default.
- Enable experiment flag for adaptive sampling on /generate and /chat-preview for next 48 hours; monitor cost-telemetry channel.

Open questions / risks:
- How do we quantify 'actionable debugging sessions' automatically? Current approach is manual annotation; need metricization for longer-term signal.
- Rolling back sampling changes may hide information needed for incident triage — mitigation: short retention snapshot for 1% requests (lightweight spans) to keep breadcrumb data.

Action items (owner — due):
- Evan: export per-route span counts and estimated per-span cost for Jan–Mar 2027 (OBS-4321) — due 2027-03-11.
- Jules: land adaptive-sampler skeleton PR + feature flag gating, include canary rollout plan — due 2027-03-12 (PR: platform/pull/1429).
- Priya: prototype dashboard widget (mock + api contract) and get PM feedback — due 2027-03-15.
- Samira: update cost-telemetry runbook with emergency throttle steps and postmortem checklist — due 2027-03-10.
- Maya: assemble Tracing BoM CSV template and seed with /embed, /generate, /chat routes — due 2027-03-09.

Runbook excerpt (emergency reduce-trace-ingestion):
1) Identify route causing spike: /internal/trace-top reported via trace-sampling-alert.
2) Use admin API to set route-sampling to 5% for 60 minutes: POST /admin/routes/<route>/sampling {"rate":0.05, "ttl_mins":60}.
3) Confirm reduction in span-counts within 2 minutes by watching `trace.ingestion.rate` metric and span pipeline lag.
4) If reduction insufficient, switch to 'header-based bypass' for critical clients only.
5) Create incident note in runbook and notify PG/sre on-call.

Experiment notes (short):
- Adaptive sampler prototype: will use reservoir sampling with rate decay based on projected cost. Need to decide decay half-life (options: 30m, 2h). Recommendation: start with 2h for smoother changes.
- Lightweight dashboard: implement aggregation at trace-collector stage to avoid rehydration costs. Store pre-aggregates in a TTL cache (6h) keyed by route+model.

Telemetry to track (weekly):
- span.count.per_route (raw)
- span.cost.estimate.per_100k
- sampled_traces.qualified_for_debugging (%) — manual annotation for now
- dashboard.embed.hits and follow-through-to-trace (%)

Notes to self / brainstorming (informal):
- Would be useful to show 'what-if' slider in BoM: move route X from 30d->7d retention and show projected $/mo delta. Could be quick UX on cost-telemetry console.
- Consider 'snapshot on error' behavior: always keep a tiny stacktrace/span bundle for requests that triggered 5xx or high-latency alerts, even if sampled otherwise. Might prevent worst-case blind spots.
- Check privacy/compliance surface: retaining smaller breadcrumb traces may still capture PII; consult security for default scrubbing policy.

Blocks / help needed:
- Need product input on which routes are 'business-critical' vs 'debug-only' so BoM tiers can be set. (Ping: @product-infra)
- Legal review on retention tiers for EU customers for BoM defaults.

Next steps for next week:
- Run adaptive-sampling canary and capture 72h trend.
- Workshop with product on BoM UI/queries.
- Postmortem writeup for the 03-06 spike including kernel/caching reproducer steps.

Appendix (quick links & scratch):
- Slack threads: #observability-traceops "model v1.8 spike" (link above).
- JIRA: OBS-4321 adaptive sampling; OBS-4360 postmortem v1.8 rollout.
- PRs: platform/pull/1429 (adaptive-sampler skeleton), ui/pull/501 (dashboard mock).

END — rough sketch. Treat as living doc; will keep iterating before turning into a polished runbook page on Confluence.
summary: Working weekly sketch for tracing BoM, adaptive sampling canary, dashboard lightweight view, runbook excerpt and action items (Maya owner).
